articles.body: GUWAHATI: Seven people, including a nightclub manager, were arrested on Saturday after a woman was allegedly “partially stripped and assaulted” by bouncers following a drunken brawl at a bar here a day earlier, police said.The arrests came after police registered a suo motu case and launched an investigation into the alleged assault at the nightclub in the Khanapara area early on Friday.The action followed the circulation of a video purportedly showing the incident on social media.The arrested people, aged between 21 and 30, include three women.Among them are the nightclub manager, event manager and a front office executive.Police are also investigating how the nightclub, ‘The Locals’, remained open well beyond its permitted closing time of 12.30am.Guwahati East deputy police commissioner Tabu Ram Pegu said police launched an inquiry after receiving information about the incident and examined the available CCTV footage."The footage revealed that the victim was assaulted inside the bar by a group of people at around 2.30 am. Thereafter, she was dragged towards the basement by pulling her hair and clothes, where she was again assaulted and appeared to become semi-conscious," Tabu told news agency PTI.Several of those allegedly involved in the incident were associated with the bar or were among its staff, Pegu said, adding that the management did not inform the local police station about the incident."Accordingly, a suo motu case was registered at the Dispur police station, and an investigation has been taken up. Seven people have been arrested so far," the DCP said.Pegu added that the police are examining the complete sequence of events, the role of each individual involved, the operation of the establishment beyond the permitted closing time, and any other violations that may emerge during the investigation.The video that surfaced online purportedly shows the woman being assaulted while lying on the floor of a building’s parking lot. Another woman is later seen intervening and coming to her rescue.According to a security guard working at the building that houses the club, the woman had hit a female bouncer with a beer bottle inside the club."This angered other bouncers there, and they brought her downstairs and assaulted her," he claimed.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: A Moroccan mine built a heavy-truck road from phosphate waste rock; field tests cut dust emissions by 91%
articles.summary: A phosphate mine in Morocco has tested a haul-road pavement made entirely from waste rock produced during phosphate extraction, according to the study.
articles.body: A phosphate mine in Morocco has tested a haul-road pavement made entirely from waste rock produced during phosphate extraction, according to the study. Researchers examined whether the material could withstand the extreme loads created by mining trucks while also reducing dust from the road surface. They designed a three-layer pavement using crushed phosphate mine waste rock and phosphated flint.According to the research published in Mining, titled ‘Innovative Pavement Design for Heavy-Haul Mining Roads Using Phosphate Mine Waste Rock: Dust Emission Control, Mechanical and Operational Performance Improvements’, the pavement included a 0.35-metre sub-base, a 0.25-metre base and a 0.07-metre asphalt wearing course.How did the Moroccan mine build a heavy-truck road from phosphate waste rockResearchers designed the pavement for a heavily trafficked haul road at the Benguerir phosphate mine. The road carries about 22.35 kilotonnes of material each day and is used by large mining trucks. The proposed structure had three layers. The sub-base was 0.35 metres thick and used crushed phosphate mine waste rock graded from 0 to 100 millimetres.The 0.25-metre base layer was made from 0 to 63-millimetre crushed screening waste rock. The surface layer was a 0.07-metre BBSG 0-20 millimetre wearing course made with phosphated flint aggregates and modified bitumen. The pavement was designed to withstand permanent deformation and structural rutting under heavy loads while controlling dust and keeping construction costs economically viable at Benguerir.How did the pavement perform under heavy mining trafficLaboratory tests were used to assess whether the proposed materials could withstand heavy mining traffic. The asphalt mixture was tested at three bitumen contents: 4.9%, 5.1%, and 5.3%. At 5.1%, the mixture reached its selected balance of mechanical and volumetric performance. It recorded a stiffness modulus of 9160 MPa and fatigue resistance of 139.6 microstrains at failure.Its proportional rut depth was 2.2%. Its apparent bulk density was 2.48 tonnes per cubic metre. Field testing then examined the bearing capacity of the compacted pavement layers. The sub-base recorded an average EV2 value of 153 MPa. The base reached 181 MPa. These measurements confirmed the load-bearing capacity recorded in the experimental pavement.The new haul-road surface reduced dust and improved visibilityThe field trial also measured dust before and after the pavement was constructed. Measurements covered PM2.5 and PM10 at two locations along the experimental haul road. The unpaved section represented the mine's existing practice, which included daily watering and routine grading. Its average dust concentration reached 91,730.16 micrograms per cubic metre. After the full pavement structure was installed, the asphalt-treated section recorded an average concentration of 8570.10 micrograms per cubic metre.The study calculated a reduction of about 91%. This exceeded OCP Group's target of reducing airborne dust emissions by more than 80%. The researchers also reported a smoother and more stable road surface after paving, with improved visibility and reduced surface roughness during truck operations.How did the paved road affect mining productivity and maintenanceThe proposed pavement was estimated to cost about €23.97 per square metre for the experimental section. The calculation included the required construction work and a 25% allowance for bulking and wastage. The study assumed the crushing unit would be within 5 kilometres of the works and the asphalt plant within 25 kilometres. After 15 months of continuous operation under actual mining traffic, an internal assessment by OCP indicated that wider use could produce an estimated annual productivity gain of about 15%.The study linked the expected gains to higher truck speeds, fewer spare-part replacements, including tyres and wheel motors, longer fleet service life and less daily haul-road maintenance.You use AI every day. articles.title: Delhi-NCR housing prices rise 12% in Q3, highest among top seven cities: Report
articles.summary: Housing prices in the Delhi-NCR primary market rose 12 per cent annually during the July-September quarter, the highest increase among India's top seven
articles.body: Housing prices in the Delhi-NCR primary market rose 12 per cent annually during the July-September quarter, the highest increase among India's top seven cities, as higher input costs and developers' growing focus on premium and luxury projects pushed up average residential prices, according to real estate consultant Anarock.Anarock data showed that the average residential property price in Delhi-NCR increased to Rs 9,980 per square foot in the September quarter from Rs 8,900 per square foot in the same period last year.Across the top seven cities, average residential prices rose 7 per cent annually to Rs 9,714 per square foot from Rs 9,105 per square foot a year earlier.The seven cities covered in the analysis are Bengaluru, Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), Delhi-NCR, Pune, Chennai, Hyderabad and Kolkata.Higher input costs push up pricesAnarock vice chairman Santhosh Kumar said housing prices had risen sharply across major cities since the Covid-19 pandemic, driven by higher input costs, including land and construction raw materials.In Delhi-NCR, Kumar said land rates in Noida, Greater Noida and Gurugram had surged, a trend reflected in auctions conducted by development authorities.He also said real estate developers were increasingly focusing on premium, luxury and ultra-luxury housing projects.The rise in average prices comes as the Delhi-NCR market continues to see demand for higher-end residential properties. Manik Malik, CEO and president of BPTP Ltd, said housing demand remained steady."In NCR, evolving infrastructure, connectivity and employment-led demand continue to support residential activity, particularly in the premium and luxury segments," Malik said, as quoted by news agency PTI.NCR prices rise despite marginal moderation in salesRobin Mangla, president of M3M India, said sales in the National Capital Region saw a marginal moderation, while the annual rise in residential prices reflected the premium commanded by well-connected micro-markets."In NCR, while sales saw a marginal moderation, the 12 per cent annual appreciation in residential prices reflects the market's continued strength and the premium commanded by well-connected micro-markets," Mangla said.Ashish Sarin, CEO and director of Alpha Corp Development Ltd, said the residential real estate market's performance in the September quarter reflected the resilience of housing demand amid changing global and economic conditions."Strong end-user demand continues to support sales, with housing increasingly being viewed as a long-term need rather than purely an investment avenue," Sarin said.According to Anarock's data, Delhi-NCR recorded the highest annual increase in average residential prices among the seven major housing markets during the July-September quarter, with prices rising 12 per cent compared with the 7 per cent increase recorded across the cities collectively.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.summary: NEW DELHI: UAE deputy prime minister Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum on Saturday met flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and praised his
articles.body: NEW DELHI: UAE deputy prime minister Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum on Saturday met flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and praised his courage, responsibility and care for human life.In a social media post on X, Hamdan bin Mohammed said that the UAE is proud that Machchhar is part of the flydubai team and part of the story of the UAE."During a visit to Captain Smit Machchhar… the flydubai pilot who embodied the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life. From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise," the UAE's Deputy Prime Minister said."We are proud that he is part of our team… part of the story of our nation… and part of what the UAE stands for… a nation of compassion… a nation of peace… and a nation of life," he added.During the flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, Machchhar was stabbed by his co-pilot, who “attempted to carry out a terrorist act” and sought to seize control of the aircraft's piloting instruments while the plane was airborne.According to the UAE's state news agency WAM, citing Attorney General Counsellor Hamad Saif al-Shamsi, the Omani co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, attacked Machchhar with a cockpit crash axe while attempting to take control of the aircraft.The assault triggered a violent struggle inside the cockpit, during which the aircraft reportedly lost about 16,000 feet in two minutes, according to reports on the incident.Machchhar, despite sustaining serious injuries, fought back and managed to unlock the cockpit door.Crew members, passengers and two off-duty pilots then entered the cockpit and helped overpower the co-pilot, allowing the aircraft to be stabilised.The flight subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 180 people on board safely disembarked.A crash axe is a standard emergency tool kept in aircraft cockpits and is designed to help pilots cut through aircraft materials during emergencies.Meanwhile, the Ministry of External Affairs said that Machchhar was recovering well in an Abu Dhabi hospital, days after being airlifted from Tabuk.The MEA said that Machchhar remained under “excellent medical care” and that it was in touch with his family and local authorities.“Indian braveheart Capt. Smit remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well. We are in touch with his family & local authorities, extending support for a speedy recovery. Our thanks to UAE gov. for their care. We join well-wishers in praying for his good health,” the Indian Embassy in UAE said in a post on X.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: An Italian family settled in America in the early 1900s; generations later, their family pepper still features in traditional recipes
articles.summary: A pepper can carry more history than its size suggests.
articles.body: A pepper can carry more history than its size suggests. For the Riccelli family, an Italian heirloom known as the ‘Ausilio Thin Skin Italian’ has remained tied to family cooking across several generations. The variety came to America with relatives whose roots were in Italy in the early 1900s, and its seeds were eventually passed down through the family rather than replaced with newer varieties. Today, the pepper still appears in recipes connected to that history, including a pork-stuffed dish based on the cooking of Nicholas Domenico “Nick” Riccelli.How one Italian family kept its pepper seeds aliveReportedly, Chad and Michele Ogle-Riccelli donated the ‘Ausilio Thin Skin Italian’ pepper to Seed Savers Exchange in 2015. Chad’s family history is connected to Giovanni “John” Ausilio and Rachel P. Scarcello, who immigrated from Italy to the United States in the early 1900s. Their daughter, Theresa Ausilio Riccelli, continued growing the family pepper. The seeds were not treated simply as something to plant for another season. They became part of a family tradition, kept and handed down alongside the recipes associated with them.It is a family seed, and preserving it means maintaining a link with relatives who are no longer alive as well as with those who still remember how it was grown and cooked.The family’s seed-saving tradition kept its old recipes aliveThe variety has remained part of the family’s culinary traditions long after the generation that first brought its Italian heritage to America. Seed saving made that possible in a very practical way. Rather than buying a replacement variety each year, the family continued to keep the seeds and grow the same type of pepper.Theresa has also remained connected to the food traditions surrounding the variety. The memories of her late husband, Nick, provide part of the story behind the stuffed-pepper recipe now associated with the family.Nick was interested in cooking and spent time with his mother-in-law, Rachel Scarcello, learning dishes from her family. Her approach to recipes was informal. Instead of measuring everything precisely, she used quantities described by hand, such as a handful or a pinch. Nick learned by cooking alongside her.The recipe begins with pork and herbsThe family recipe collected by Seed Savers Exchange uses six to eight of the peppers. They are filled with a mixture based on one pound of ground pork, along with garlic, salt, pepper, basil and parsley. Bread crumbs moistened with a little milk are added to the mixture, followed by two eggs. The filling also contains freshly shredded Parmigiano-Reggiano and Romano cheese. It is a fairly substantial combination, designed to sit inside the peppers rather than simply accompany them.The preparation is straightforward. The peppers are cleaned, their seeds removed and the pork mixture packed inside. They are then placed in a baking dish and covered with sauce. There is room for a family variation, too. The Riccellis sometimes add medium-sized pieces of diced potato to the dish before it goes into the oven.Baking the stuffed peppersThe oven is heated to 420°F, or about 215°C. The stuffed peppers first bake in their sauce for around 30 minutes. At that stage, fresh mozzarella and basil are added. The dish then returns to the oven for another 15 minutes, or until the pork is cooked through. The total cooking time is therefore roughly 45 minutes.The recipe serves about six people and reflects the kind of cooking that can be adjusted according to what is available. Even the original instructions retain the family's informal character, with ingredients described in handfuls and pinches rather than converted into strict measurements.Preserving the pepper kept its family history intactThe ‘Ausilio Thin Skin Italian’ pepper is now preserved outside the Riccelli family as well, but its importance to the family came first. Chad and Michele's decision to donate the variety to Seed Savers Exchange gave it a place in a wider collection of heirloom seeds while retaining its connection to their own history.For the family, saving the pepper is closely tied to the people who grew it. Chad has described the seeds as belonging to his grandmother's family and as something special enough to pass to future generations.The pepper's name also preserves part of that story. “Ausilio” comes from the family line connected to Giovanni Ausilio and Theresa Ausilio Riccelli, while the variety itself remains associated with the cooking that developed around it in America.You use AI every day. articles.body: Six people are missing after a Gulfstream G100 jet traveling from Bermuda to Boston lost contact with air traffic controllers early Saturday, triggering a Coast Guard search off the coast of Nantucket.The aircraft, carrying six people, was flying toward Boston when it disappeared from radar, with the US Coast Guard launching air and surface crews to search for the plane, the New York Post reported, citing Coast Guard and flight-tracking information.The Coast Guard said it was notified that contact with the aircraft had been lost and that crews from Air Station Cape Cod, US Coast Guard Station Brant Point in Nantucket and the USCGC William Sparling were involved in the search.Flight-tracking data showed the Gulfstream G100, identified by tail number CGRJP, was traveling from Bermuda to Boston. Its final known position was off the coast of Nantucket, according to flight-tracking data.“Air & surface crews have launched in search of the aircraft. articles.summary: Russia on Saturday warned foreign diplomats and nationals to leave Kyiv and said it would continue targeted strikes on the Ukrainian capital, hours after
articles.body: Russia on Saturday warned foreign diplomats and nationals to leave Kyiv and said it would continue targeted strikes on the Ukrainian capital, hours after a Russian attack damaged the Northern Bridge. Ukrainian authorities reported six deaths across the country.The Russian foreign ministry said Moscow was responding to what it called Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilians and infrastructure.“In response to the Ukrainian Armed Forces' terrorist acts against the civilian population and civilian infrastructure of our country, the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation are continuing to systematically carry out targeted strikes on military facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities,” it said.The ministry again urged foreign nationals, including diplomatic staff, against staying in or travelling to Ukraine.“We note with concern that not everyone has heeded these warnings, and that individuals are knowingly exposing themselves to mortal danger,” it said, according to AFP.Additionally, the ministry informed that, “responsibility for any potential negative consequences rests entirely with those who ignore this warning.”The warning came as an attack on Kyiv’s Northern Bridge damaged the road surface and trolleybus cables and disrupted traffic, according to Kyiv mayor Vitalii Klitschko. Two people were wounded, he said, with one briefly hospitalised.Russia’s defence ministry confirmed it carried out the strike, saying the bridge was used to “facilitate troop movements and the logistics of military cargo deliveries” for Ukraine’s armed forces.The latest warning comes as Kyiv faces repeated aerial attacks, with air raid alerts disrupting daily life in the city of about three million people. Russia had issued a similar warning in May.On Friday, Klitschko said Kyiv was in a “very dramatic situation” and should be on a war footing as the enemy was “tearing Kyiv apart” with strikes on bridges and energy infrastructure.Elsewhere, Russian attacks on Kharkiv and nearby areas killed five people and wounded more than 40, according to regional governor Oleh Syniehubov. Russian drone strikes in Izyum wounded three people, local authorities said.In Odesa, a sailor was killed and three others wounded after Russian forces struck a civilian cargo ship, the Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority said.Moldovan president Maia Sandu said the conflict was “dangerously reaching” her country after what she said were Russian airspace incursions.“I condemn Russia’s attack on Ukraine this morning. Its war is dangerously reaching Moldova,” Sandu said.Both Russia and Ukraine deny deliberately targeting civilians. The latest strikes come as diplomatic efforts to end the war remain stalled.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 50 cities, 70,000 protesters: Spain’s housing crisis fuels nationwide anger
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets in Madrid and other Spanish cities on Saturday, stepping up demands for action on the country's housing
articles.body: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets in Madrid and other Spanish cities on Saturday, stepping up demands for action on the country's housing crisis after parliament rejected government measures aimed at protecting renters and addressing rising housing costs.The protests followed Friday's defeat of the emergency measures, which had been introduced after the eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid triggered widespread public anger. Some protesters in Madrid carried posters calling for a general strike.Around 70,000 people participated in the Madrid demonstration, according to the Spanish government. Protests were also held in around 50 other cities."It's a shame," said Nando de Anguulo, 26, who joined the Madrid protest."It only proves that it is us the people who have to adapt to the political parties, and not the politicians to what the people want, and this can't go on like that", Angulo added, as quoted by Reuters.Housing measures rejected in parliamentThe government measures included provisions aimed at preventing the eviction of vulnerable people, discouraging property speculation and providing tax incentives to encourage renting.A second decree sought to make residential leases automatically renewable by tenants, according to news agency AP.The measures were rejected after the Catalan separatist party Junts voted against them, alongside the centre-right Popular Party and far-right Vox. Other smaller parties also opposed the second decree.Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez had appealed to lawmakers to approve the measures, describing them as necessary during a five-hour parliamentary debate.“What is behind these decrees is the desire to instill order and a sense of humanity in a market that if we do not rein it in will destroy our society,” Sánchez said.“What is behind these decrees is the desire to instill order and a sense of humanity in a market that if we do not rein it in will destroy our society,” Sánchez said.Sánchez concluded his appeal by telling lawmakers: “Do the right thing, or history will judge you, and sooner than you think”.The defeat has also triggered speculation in Spanish media that Sánchez could call an early election in November, ahead of the election scheduled for next year.Rent costs have nearly doubled in a decadeThe protests have highlighted the wider pressure on Spain's housing market, where rents have risen sharply over the past decade.The average rent in Spain has almost doubled in the past 10 years, while the average price per square metre increased from 8.20 euros in 2016 to 15.1 euros this year, according to real estate website Idealista.Spain's government has said 26 per cent of people who rent spend an average of 40 per cent of their income on rent and utilities, compared with an EU average of 18 per cent of renters.Government-owned rental housing accounts for less than 2 per cent of Spain's available housing stock, compared with an EU average of 8 per cent.The housing crisis has particularly affected people who cannot afford to buy homes and are dependent on the country's relatively limited rental market.Eviction of 87-year-old woman sparks protestsThe latest wave of demonstrations followed the eviction of María del Carmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman who had lived in her Madrid home for seven decades.Around 1,000 protesters had spent the previous week camping at Madrid's Puerta del Sol, demanding stronger protections for tenants.The company that evicted Abascal eventually agreed to allow her to return to the apartment following public and political pressure. She remained in hospital after being removed from her home on a stretcher, while her lawyer said she was happy to know she would be able to return.The eviction turned Abascal into a symbol of the campaign against rising housing costs, with protesters carrying signs such as "Not even one more Maricarmen!"Protests spread beyond MadridSaturday's demonstrations were largely peaceful, although clashes were reported in Valencia, where police fired rubber bullets and tear gas to disperse protesters.About 30 protesters entered the City of Arts and Sciences, a landmark cultural complex, before being removed by police. Demonstrations elsewhere were peaceful.The renters association Sindicato de Inquilinas, which has led calls for action, had urged people to join Saturday's demonstrations and was also pushing for a general strike.The group and other protesters have blamed property speculators for rising prices and have called for stronger measures to protect tenants.The government now faces the choice of pursuing fresh legislation after the defeat of its emergency measures or considering an early election, with Spanish media reporting that Sánchez could be weighing the latter option.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: St. Louis man Michael Goessling was adopted nearly 60 years ago; after an unknown half-brother took a 23andMe test, he learned five-time Grammy winner Michael McDonald was his biological father
articles.summary: A St. Louis man who was adopted as a baby nearly 60 years ago has discovered that five-time Grammy Award winner Michael McDonald is his biological father.
articles.body: A St. Louis man who was adopted as a baby nearly 60 years ago has discovered that five-time Grammy Award winner Michael McDonald is his biological father. Michael Goessling always knew he had been adopted and said he had a “wonderful childhood” with the couple who raised him. But he continued to wonder about his biological parents and where they were.The mystery began to unravel decades later after a half-brother Goessling did not know existed took a 23andMe DNA test. The test connected the two men and led to a message that changed Goessling’s understanding of his family. “Within 36 hours, he got an email notifying him, ‘Michael Gossling, half brother, St. Louis,’” Goessling said. “And that’s how this all began,” he told WSAW.The discovery eventually led Goessling to his birth mother. On his 58th birthday, he met her in person for the first time. He later spoke with his biological father over the phone. During that conversation, Goessling asked about his father’s work. He was told that his biological father was a musician who was preparing to tour through St. Louis that summer.That answer led Goessling to ask a question that would finally reveal the identity of his biological father. “And I said, ‘Are you Michael McDonald?’” Goessling said. “And he said, ‘Yeah, I’m afraid so.’” The musician was indeed McDonald, the singer-songwriter and member of the Doobie Brothers known for songs including “What a Fool Believes” and “I Keep Forgettin’.”A long-standing family mysteryGoessling said he had always known he was adopted. He was raised by his adoptive parents, Paul and Kay, in St. Louis, and described his childhood as a happy one.“Always knew I was adopted,” Goessling said. “I had a wonderful childhood. I could not have handpicked two finer folks to raise me.”Even with that happy childhood, he remained curious about his biological family. That question stayed with him for decades before the 23andMe test taken by his previously unknown half-brother brought the first major breakthrough.The test identified Goessling as a half-brother and gave him a connection to a part of his biological family that he had never known. From there, he was able to meet his birth mother and later speak to his biological father.Goessling’s biological parents were both 14 years old when he was conceived, according to the information provided by KMOV. Although they did not raise him, McDonald and Goessling’s biological mother remained close friends over the years.There was also an unusual coincidence in the family discovery. Goessling and McDonald share the same first name, but that was not because Goessling was named after the musician. Goessling explained that he had been unnamed at birth and was given his name by his adoptive mother, Kay.Michael McDonald talks about the years of uncertaintyFor McDonald, finding out what had happened to his son after so many years brought a different set of emotions. He said he had spent decades wondering about him and carried guilt over not knowing how his life had turned out.“We always talked about him. But just to know that he was ok and that he had a good life, and a life certainly that I wouldn’t have been able to afford him at that time, was a great reward.”McDonald also spoke about the role of Goessling’s adoptive parents in his life. He praised them for raising him and providing him with a happy childhood. “The real rock stars in this story are his adoptive parents,” McDonald said.Goessling and McDonald eventually met in person, turning the DNA discovery into a face-to-face family reunion.Father and son meet for the first timeWhen Goessling and McDonald finally met, their first interaction was an embrace. Goessling recalled that McDonald opened his arms, gave him a “big old bear hug” and told him he loved him. “He just put his arms out, just gave me a big old bear hug and told me he loved me, and I told him the same,” Goessling said.McDonald also described the meeting as an emotional moment after years of not knowing what had happened to his son. “It was a wonderful, wonderful experience to see Michael and get to meet my son after all these years thinking about him,” McDonald said.The reunion also brought another unexpected change for McDonald. Meeting Goessling meant discovering that he had grandchildren. “Yeah, that’s still sinking in for me. articles.title: Wisconsin diver Mark Schachtner was searching Pewaukee Lake for old bottles when he spotted a 17-foot canoe 15 feet underwater; radiocarbon dating has now confirmed it is about 1,000 years old
articles.summary: An ordinary dive in search of old bottles has led to an extraordinary archaeological discovery beneath a Wisconsin lake.
articles.body: An ordinary dive in search of old bottles has led to an extraordinary archaeological discovery beneath a Wisconsin lake. Mark Schachtner, a diver from Beaver Dam, spotted a partially buried 17-foot dugout canoe while exploring Pewaukee Lake in May. Radiocarbon dating has since established that the vessel is about 1,000 years old. According to the Wisconsin Historical Society, the canoe dates to the Late Woodland period and is made of white oak. The Society is consulting with Native Nations and archaeological experts to document the discovery, while the canoe will remain submerged rather than being removed from the lake.Diver searching for bottles finds an ancient canoeSchachtner has been diving in southeastern Wisconsin for about a decade and regularly explores lakes with the Four Seasons Dive Club, often looking for old embossed glass bottles. During a dive in Pewaukee Lake in early May, however, he noticed what appeared to be a much older object resting on the lake bottom.Schachtner told Wisconsin Public Radio (WPR) that the canoe was the oldest human-made object he had ever found. He had previously discovered a fossil while diving in another lake, but the canoe represented an entirely different kind of find.The vessel was lying about 15 feet beneath the surface and was partially filled with sediment. Schachtner recognised it as a dugout canoe because he had previously worked with Tamara Thomsen, a maritime archaeologist with the Wisconsin Historical Society who has studied ancient canoes in Wisconsin. Within days of the discovery, Thomsen joined Schachtner at the site. She and the team recorded measurements, photographs and video and collected wood samples for further analysis. Thomsen described the discovery to WPR as a “beautiful find” and noted that the canoe remained intact on the lake bottom.Radiocarbon dating places it around 1,000 years agoThe wood was identified as white oak by Michael Wiemann at the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Forest Products Laboratory in Madison. The species is also found in several other ancient canoes previously documented in Lake Mendota.A sample was then analysed by Beta Analytic, a radiocarbon-dating laboratory in Miami. The results indicated a 70% probability that the canoe was in use between A.D. 992 and 1049, placing it roughly 1,000 years ago. The period corresponds to Wisconsin's Late Woodland period.Researchers also found evidence of how the canoe was made. Thomsen told WPR that char marks were visible on its underside, while scraping marks appeared consistent with shaping using stone tools or shells. The findings offer clues about the methods used by Indigenous canoe makers during the period.Why the canoe may have been intentionally submergedThe canoe's condition and position have also provided clues about how it may have been used. Thomsen told WPR that the way the vessel was sitting in the sediment was characteristic of a canoe that had been deliberately cached. According to Thomsen, Indigenous people commonly sank canoes into lakebeds and allowed them to fill with sediment. They could later retrieve the vessels, let them dry somewhat and return them to use. This practice would have helped preserve and store heavy wooden canoes that were difficult to move over land.Larry Plucinski, a tribal historic preservation officer for the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa, told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that dugout canoes were a primary form of transportation during the period and were generally used by the broader community rather than being individually owned. He explained that their weight made them difficult to carry over land, making it practical to leave them near the water for later use.Jon Greendeer, president of the Ho-Chunk Nation, told WPR that the discovery falls within Ho-Chunk territory and that he was excited by the find. He also said that finding canoes and other Indigenous artifacts in the area was not unexpected. Greendeer described canoe construction as a labour-intensive process, noting that the vessels were crafted by carving wood using fire and other tools.Canoe will remain underwaterThe discovery adds to Wisconsin's growing record of ancient dugout canoes. State archaeologists and volunteers have examined 88 out of 130 known vessels on lake bottoms and within collections across the state, said Thomsen. Thomsen said Wisconsin has half of the top 10 oldest canoes in eastern North America. The Pewaukee Lake canoe is actually the second ancient canoe known to have been found there. According to Thomsen's research into historical newspaper accounts, another canoe was discovered and removed from the lake in the 1930s.Unlike the previously recovered vessels from Lake Mendota, however, the newly identified canoe is not currently being removed. The Wisconsin Historical Society is consulting with Native Nations, including the Ho-Chunk Nation, and the decision is to leave the canoe in place out of respect for Indigenous ancestors. The site is protected under Wisconsin law, and divers are prohibited from removing archaeological objects.Leaving the canoe submerged also protects the fragile wood. The Wisconsin Historical Society notes that an ancient wooden canoe can deteriorate rapidly once exposed to air unless it undergoes an intensive preservation process, such as the treatment used for canoes recovered from Lake Mendota.For now, the 17-foot vessel remains on the bottom of Pewaukee Lake, offering archaeologists and Native Nations another opportunity to study how Indigenous communities lived, travelled and used Wisconsin's waterways roughly a millennium ago.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'No deadline for Sheikh Hasina's return', says Indian high commissioner in Bangladesh
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh on Saturday said Dhaka’s extradition request for ousted ex-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was being
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh on Saturday said Dhaka’s extradition request for ousted ex-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was being legally examined, so New Delhi could not state a deadline for her return.“Nobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasina’s return),” High commissioner Dinesh Trivedi remarked during a discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. PTI reported.“Again and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,” Trivedi added.Hasina sought asylum in India after a massive anti-establishment agitation led to the collapse of her government in August 2024.Trivedi said New Delhi had no role in Hasina’s extraction. She was escorted by a Bangladeshi military detachment from her residence and brought to India through a Bangladeshi aircraft.“At that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that”, Trivedi said.Trivedi alleged the situation emerged because of “tragic circumstances” in Bangladesh, adding that such circumstances should never be repeated anywhere in the world.“What was our choice?” Trivedi asked, pointing at the uncertainty of the potential situation, had India denied entry to Hasina’s aircraft.Strained tiesIndia-Bangladesh ties severely deteriorated after Hasina sought asylum in Delhi.Hasina was replaced by an interim government led by Mohammad Yunus, which repeatedly called for her extraction from India.During that 18-month interim rule, Hasina was tried in absentia by a special tribunal and sentenced to death; her Awami League party was also disbanded.Following the February 12 elections, Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) came to power. Its government endorsed the ban on Hasina's party and repeatedly renewed the demand for her extradition.However, relations never fully recovered despite a new government in Bangladesh.They were strained further when Hasina addressed a virtual press conference from New Delhi on 5 August 2026, the second anniversary of her removal from power. Bangladesh's foreign ministry had earlier said that the atmosphere for Rahman's visit had been "vitiated" by Hasina's virtual press interaction.India has maintained that it had no role in the media event and that it does not endorse anything said at the forum about the Bangladesh government.Rahman had declined the invitation to attend the BRICS outreach summit, while a separate bilateral invitation has been on hold since February.Despite the downturn in bilateral relations, Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, said after meeting Trivedi on Tuesday that Dhaka was "positive" about progress in discussions on Rahman's proposed visit to India; PTI reported that no date has been fixed yet.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Launched in 2020, Minecraft's Uncensored Library held around 300 books; RSF continues adding censored journalism
articles.summary: What happens to a news story after authorities block or censor it? It can find another home inside a video game.
articles.body: What happens to a news story after authorities block or censor it? It can find another home inside a video game. In 2020, Reporters Without Borders (RSF), working with Minecraft design collective BlockWorks, launched the Uncensored Library, a vast digital archive built inside Minecraft. The project turns censored journalism into in-game books, allowing players to read reporting that may be restricted in the countries where it was originally published. The library has continued to grow. In its 2026 update, RSF added a new United States room and expanded sections dedicated to Egypt, Belarus, Russia and Iran, bringing journalism from 10 countries into the collection.What the Uncensored Library is and why Reporters Without Borders built it in MinecraftMinecraft calls the Uncensored Library a grand digital library meant to combat censorship. Created by the organisation Reporters Without Borders and the Minecraft design collective BlockWorks, it was first introduced in 2020. Its purpose was to give silenced authors a platform in their own respective countries, among those that seek to censor their citizens or prevent them from accessing certain information. The University of North Carolina at Charlotte's library guide, written by Erika Boardman and published in 2022, adds that the library gives access to journal articles that were deemed forbidden, and that Reporters Without Borders strives to fight global censorship.Why a video game? How Minecraft stays reachable when other platforms are blockedThe platform itself matters. As per Minecraft, social media and other platforms tend to be either blocked or controlled in the countries concerned, while Minecraft often remains accessible. That gave Reporters Without Borders a way to circumvent the censorship and make information accessible. The University of North Carolina at Charlotte's library calls Minecraft a popular open-world game and describes its use as a unique way to reach the younger population, while providing access to information that was condemned and hidden from the public. The finished project is a blocky book bastion, a playful phrase for a serious aim.How to visit the Uncensored Library, from the Minecraft server to the downloadable mapMinecraft's article says the library is accessed through a Minecraft server, and that it can also be downloaded locally from the website. The University of North Carolina at Charlotte's library guide confirms that the website explains how to access the library in Minecraft. Yet, it comes with a limitation, the library is available to Windows and Mac users, but console players are out of luck, as the guide apologises to them. Anyone planning a visit should therefore read the website's instructions before setting up.Around 300 books, twelve wings and a statue of a clenched hand holding a penAccording to Minecraft, the library holds around 300 books distributed between twelve wings, most of them represented by a country where information may be limited. Visitors can wander through and read banned articles presented as Minecraft books. The screenshots published in Minecraft's article offer glimpses of the setting that include a statue outside the library depicting a clenched hand with a pen, an exterior park, a book being read inside, and an Arabian floor design within the building. The imagery in the game world gives a real sense of scale, from the statue to the park.How the countries and articles were picked, from the Press Freedom Index to journalists' own submissionsMinecraft explains that the countries in the library were selected with the help of Google Analytics, by looking at countries with an active Minecraft community as well as the Press Freedom Index published by Reporters Without Borders. Once a list had been drawn up, journalists from each of those countries then provided their articles, which were transformed into Minecraft books. The University of North Carolina at Charlotte's library says the books come from countries ranked poorly on a freedom index and include work by journalists who fought to uncover and share the truth and paid an unfortunate price for doing so. Minecraft also describes the collection as carefully curated.New rooms for Brazil, Belarus, Eritrea and Iran, how the library keeps growingThe Uncensored Library is regularly expanded by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), making it a collection that continues to evolve rather than a fixed archive. In its March 2026 update, RSF said the library had added a new room dedicated to the United States, while also expanding the Egypt, Belarus, Russia and Iran sections. The Belarus room received six new articles, the Russia section gained more than 20 articles from exiled media outlets, and the Egypt and Iran rooms also received new material. RSF said the library then featured journalism from Egypt, Belarus, Brazil, Eritrea, Iran, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam and the United States.The project also goes beyond Minecraft's usual role as a space for building and creativity. RSF created the virtual library as a way for journalists to make censored articles accessible, using a platform that is freely available in many countries where independent news websites may be blocked. The articles appear as books inside Minecraft and are available in English as well as the authors' native languages. Since its opening in 2020, RSF said the library had been visited more than one million times, and its books had been read 10 million times.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In California, an architect spent 27 years turning his backyard into a miniature Disneyland with a working skyway, castle and railroad then opened it free to visitors
articles.summary: Discover the incredible 27-year journey of David Sheegog, whose backyard transformation into a miniature Disneyland features a working skyway, castle, and railroad. Open to the public, this tribute to Disney's legacy captivates visitors with unique architecture and special effects.
articles.body: A miniature rendition of Disneyland Resort and various Disney animated films have been realised through the backyard of an Independent architect as reported by the LA Times. Built over 27 years of manual construction, the private garden is an exhibition of large architectural models, operational model trains, and live special effects. Officially known as Castle Peak and Thunder Railroad, the highly detailed microcosm serves as a tribute to classic animation and regional theme park history. The setting is particularly fitting: Anaheim's identity changed dramatically after Disneyland opened in 1955, which turned the city into a major destination for tourism.This backyard creation was conceived by 70-year-old Anaheim Hills resident, David Sheegog, who began its planning in 1997. The project began as a small model railroad on his dining room table, with an intended timeline of 10 years, and was meant to serve as an educational problem-solving endeavor for his children. Although his children are all grown up, Sheegog continues to expand the backyard layout and as of today, the family’s private property is open to the public for brief free-admission open houses each spring and fall. However, owing to intense regional demand, it takes only a minute for all 250 reservation slots per date to routinely disappear.Architectural scale and the engineering behind it In lieu of using store-bought plastic kits, every architectural landmark in the layout has been built from scratch. The exhibit’s centerpiece is a seven-foot-tall replica of the Sleeping Beauty Castle made over time using PVC, wood turnings, and cast resin veneer, then later updated with custom 3D-printed materials and polyurethane foam boards. Clustered around are large models of other renowned Disney staples: a Victorian train station, a Haunted Mansion, Beast's Castle, Rapunzel's Tower, Prince Eric's Seaside Villa, and Carl Fredricksen's house from Up.Beyond the centerpiece, the park is fully operational with a transit system that features a custom garden railroad network and an aerial skyway sourced directly from Von Roll Model Ropeways. To add more theatrical flair and breathe life into it, Sheegog included automated multi-sensory special effects. There’s a tiny Casey Jr. Circus Train that crosses a stone bridge and, in doing so, plays its classic theme song from a built-in sound module. In addition, a custom "enchanted tiki waterbar" is built directly into the patio with a dedicated pump and water reservoir that suddenly triggers a lightning, thunder, and rain show across a glass viewing window.Deep Cultural Preservation and what the Future entails Besides the tangible replicas of the theme park landmarks, the estate exists as an expansive visual archive of animation history. Sheegog has filled the estate with subtle hidden references to 80 individual Disney and Pixar animated films released between 1937 (Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs) and 2021 (Encanto) but the layout is reaching its physical capacity and he intends to close it off.Sheegog estimates that over the last over the years his cumulative financial investment equals the cost it would take to install a standard backyard pool. Factoring all the massive labor costs, the cost of building a single castle sets the bill at approximately $70,000. Over the years, the backyard project has become a beacon of the community for Southern California residents, many of whom spent their lives near Disneyland and now compete for open house reservations.Looking ahead to his retirement, Sheegog is already vying for major new expansion, working from inside his garage workshop on a model for an entryway and plans to move the Sheegog home's retaining wall. For this project, the inspiration comes from Disneyland's Mine Train Through Nature's Wonderland and the modern Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge expansion.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 1583, stone from a ruined Welsh castle was used to build this mansion; 400 years later, a couple bought it for £750,000 and restored it
articles.summary: The historic Y Fan mansion in Caerphilly, South Wales, has a past that reaches back to the Tudor period.
articles.body: The historic Y Fan mansion in Caerphilly, South Wales, has a past that reaches back to the Tudor period. Parts of the Grade II-listed house were rebuilt in 1583 using dressed stone taken from nearby Caerphilly Castle, which was then largely derelict. Centuries later, the mansion itself had fallen into serious disrepair. In 2017, London couple Christine Tallon and Adrian Cole bought it for £750,000 and began a demanding restoration. Their work eventually turned the neglected property into a 7-room bed and breakfast, and in 2026 the restored mansion was placed on the market for £1.5 million.How did the 1583 Welsh mansion gain stone from Caerphilly CastleY Fan has a recorded history dating to 1529, when Edward Lewis, sheriff of Glamorgan and a prominent landowner, acquired a house on the site. The Gatehouse Gazetteer records that the original building included a ground-floor hall and a storeyed porch, with a two-storey kitchen wing added during the 16th century.In 1583, Edward Lewis's son Thomas secured a lease of Caerphilly Castle from the Earl of Pembroke. He then used dressed stone from the castle to rebuild parts of Van House, including a new stair block, gatehouse and walled court. The material came from the castle when it was already in a neglected state. The Gatehouse Gazetteer identifies the surviving property as one of the important Tudor mansions of Glamorgan, despite the extensive restoration it has undergone.BBC later reported that the connection can still be seen in the mansion itself, particularly around its corners, where some of the reused castle stone remains visible. The house therefore carries pieces of Caerphilly Castle within its own walls.The house had a long decline before its modern restorationY Fan did not remain at the centre of the Lewis family's life forever. According to the Gatehouse Gazetteer, Sir Edward Lewis transferred his seat to St Fagans Castle in 1616. After the main family line was no longer based in Glamorgan, Van House became less important. The property eventually passed into the Plymouth Estate and was leased to tenants.Over time, parts of the building were altered, extended or dismantled. By 1991, the Gatehouse record notes that some of the lower-storey windows had been removed and only the bases of the attic windows survived. The building was later thoroughly restored, helping to preserve its Tudor character.That long period of decline meant the mansion was in very poor condition when Tallon and Cole encountered it. BBC reported that by 2017 it was damp and mouldy, with mushrooms growing inside.Why did a London couple take on the neglected propertyChristine Tallon and Adrian Cole had been living and working in Bexley, south-east London. Tallon was a lawyer and Cole a finance director, and the couple wanted a different pace of life.BBC reported that their city careers had left them spending much of their time either working or commuting. They were not initially searching for a major restoration project. Instead, they saw Y Fan as a property that could potentially become a bed and breakfast.After viewing the mansion 8 times, however, they decided to take it on. They bought it for £750,000 and began the restoration, despite Cole having no previous renovation experience.The scale of the task quickly became clear. The house had 132 windows that needed refurbishment, while its tall ceilings meant that even changing a light bulb could require scaffolding. The damp and mould affecting the large rooms added another layer of work.The restoration turned the old mansion into a B&BWork began in 2018, with the couple tackling the building themselves while also dealing with the demands of restoring a historic property. A later account of the project described the building as having required extensive attention to its walls, ceilings, heating, plumbing and electrics.The renovation was originally expected to lead to a B&B opening in summer 2020. The Covid-19 pandemic disrupted those plans, however, and the opening was pushed back.According to the BBC, Y Fan finally opened with 7 rooms in May 2021. The restored property retained its historic identity while taking on a new role as accommodation for visitors.What happens next for the 500-year-old propertyAfter years of work, the couple decided it was time to move on. In June 2026, the BBC reported that Y Fan was being offered for £1.5 million, twice the price the couple paid for it in 2017. They have not disclosed how much they spent on the restoration.The decision was linked to the demands of running a hospitality business from such a large historic house. Tallon told the BBC that they were getting older and that hospitality was more demanding than many people might expect. The work carried out by Tallon and Cole gave Y Fan a new use without erasing the history embedded in its structure.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

Police have arrested four persons, including three juveniles. The primary accused, identified as Bhuvan, remains at large.The deceased, Yogesh, a resident of Nagadevanahalli, was studying in his first year of BCom at a private college in Nagarabhavi. On learning about this, an enraged Bhuvan instigated one of the juveniles to take revenge on Yogesh.He and the juvenile assembled a group of youths from Laggere and called Yogesh around 2.15pm to meet near a local gym behind the college campus. When Yogesh arrived at the spot along with his classmate, Bhuvan and his associates confronted him regarding the comments. An argument broke out and quickly turned violent. During the clash, one of the juveniles took out a knife, which was purchased online, and plunged it into Yogesh’s chest, a senior officer said.His classmate and another friend rushed Yogesh to a nearby private hospital, where he was declared brought dead. articles.summary: IUML review meet in Malappuram urges ministers and MLAs to avoid lavishness, stay humble, be cautious in media/social posts, and focus on development plans.
articles.body: Kozhikode: IUML has instructed its elected representatives to avoid lavishness and interact with the public with humility. Party functionaries also urged them to avoid arrogance of power in their work and focus more on development activities.The directions were issued to ministers and MLAs at a review meeting held at Safi College in Vazhayur, Malappuram. The meeting, held from 10am to noon, assessed the performance of the party’s elected representatives so far.IUML state president Panakkad Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal advised ministers and elected representatives to exercise caution while speaking in public and before the media. He urged them to avoid controversies, maintain their connect with the people and ensure that their statements were not open to misinterpretation by the public. He also asked them to be more careful with their social media posts and public interactions.Experts conducted orientation classes on development projects to be undertaken in the constituencies and across the state. The party directed its representatives to prepare development plans based on the discussions.The meeting of elected representatives, including ministers, called by the party brass assumed significance in the backdrop of recent controversies involving the party and its ministers. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Saturday slammed Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah "illegal" and accused the Congress of disrespecting the Constitution.In a statement, the Union minister described the statement an insult to constitutional institutions and electoral mandate of the people."The statement made by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at the direction of leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi is yet another example of their frustration, defeatist mindset and the Congress party's longstanding practice of attacking constitutional institutions," Chouhan said in a statement."Kharge calling the Prime Minister and the home minister 'illegal' is an insult to constitutional institutions and the mandate of the people," he said.This comes after Kharge demanded dissolving the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies, saying that all the elections were illegal and even Prime Minister Modi, home minister Amit Shah and chief ministers of all the states were illegal."Today, the entire country is being run on illegal elections. Modi is an illegal Prime Minister, Shah is an illegal minister, and all the chief ministers who have been elected anywhere are illegal. All of them should be dissolved, elections should be held, and elections should be conducted through ballot papers," he said.He alleged that the ongoing SIR of the electoral roll has many irregularities and is undermining democracy, pointing out that the government is making many mistakes in the process.Kharge pointed out that under the new law, if the CEC or our Election Commissioners commit any mistake, "there can be no inquiry against them anywhere -- till death", alleging that this is how they were destroying democracy.Referring to a report by The Indian Express on the SIR, Kharge said that two members of the Election Commission had written to the Chief Election Commissioner 10 and 14 times, respectively, but their letters had no impact."They cannot speak openly outside, but they expressed their views clearly, he said, adding that if such things continue, they can conduct elections arbitrarily."We have to see whether you want to save democracy in this country or destroy it. articles.title: Chhattisgarh: Potash bombs emerge as new poaching threat in Udanti Tiger Reserve; 2 held with 13 live devices
articles.summary: Raipur: Explosives are emerging as a disturbing new tool for wildlife hunting in and around Chhattisgarh's Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve, with the
articles.body: Raipur: Explosives are emerging as a disturbing new tool for wildlife hunting in and around Chhattisgarh's Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve, with the anti-poaching unit uncovering fresh evidence of potash bombs being used to kill wild animals along the Chhattisgarh-Odisha border.In the latest operation, two men from Odisha’s Nabarangpur district were caught in the Chikhlapani area of Risgaon range after they were found cutting up the carcass of a wild boar hunted using explosives. Two others fled from the spot.Forest teams seized 13 live potash bombs, along with a tangia, knife, sickle, katta and other hunting implements. The accused were identified as Narsingh, and Mansingh, both residents of Khiloli village in Nabarangpur. They were produced before a JMFC court at Nagri on Oct 1 and remanded to judicial custody.A forest offence has been registered under the Wildlife (Protection) Act. A third person, Bharat Rathore of Kohrabeda in Kondagaon district, suspected of supplying explosive material, has been served a notice under BNS because of health-related circumstances.The case has reinforced USTR’s concern that potash bombs are no longer isolated improvised devices but part of a broader hunting practice. Field intelligence suggests that more than 20 people have previously been caught or detained for alleged involvement in the use or manufacture of explosives for wildlife hunting in and around the reserve.In an earlier case involving a suspect from Nagri in Dhamtari, a search had led to the recovery of a large quantity of suspected explosive material along with 86 sloth-bear claws, pointing to the use of locally available explosives alongside conventional hunting weapons.The latest investigation widened further after a search linked to one of the accused yielded 29 cartridges, two bomb/firecracker-type articles, 20 explosive crackers and several packets of suspected explosive material. Investigators are now examining whether the material was part of a larger chain of procurement, storage and supply.USTR has also decided to pursue parallel action under the explosive substances Act, wherever evidence supports illegal possession, manufacture or use of explosives, in addition to wildlife offences.Officials say the danger goes beyond poaching. Potash bombs can explode when consumed or triggered by an animal, causing indiscriminate injury or death not only to wildlife but also to livestock and forest or police patrol teams.The reserve has identified the Keshkal-Kanker-Nabarangpur-Nagri belt as a hotspot and warned that repeated poaching and disturbance can also push injured or frightened animals towards farms and settlements, potentially worsening human-wildlife conflict.The Sept 29 operation was carried out with cyber support from Gariyaband police and field inputs from USTR’s anti-poaching network. articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh physiotherapists shine at World Physiotherapy AWP 2026 in Delhi, with 60-70 attending; AP member honoured at paediatric CPG launch.
articles.body: Vijayawada: Andhra Pradesh’s physiotherapy community made a strong mark at the world physiotherapy Asia Western Pacific (AWP) regional conference 2026 in New Delhi, with around 60-70 physiotherapists, students, clinicians and academicians from the state actively participating in the international event.The prestigious event was recently held at Yashobhoomi (IICC); the conference brought together more than 10,000 experts from India and abroad. Themed “Fitness for All: Empowering Communities, Building Inclusive Health!”, the conference focused on the evolving role of physiotherapy in clinical practice, education and public health.The conference was inaugurated by Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta and NCAHP chairperson Yagna Shukla. Prime Minister Narendra Modi sent a virtual message congratulating physiotherapists. Delhi CM Gupta described physiotherapists as the “healing hands” of the healthcare system.The Andhra Pradesh contingent participated in academic, cultural and sporting events, including the Global Parade and Physio baton. AP State executive committee member Sree Rajya Lakshmi Vemula was honoured during the launch of the Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPG) for Pediatric Conditions for her contribution as an author. “The conference has provided a valuable platform for physiotherapists to exchange knowledge, present research and understand emerging trends in clinical practice. Its focus on fitness for all and inclusive healthcare highlights the need to bridge gaps in access and knowledge and ensure quality physiotherapy services for every section of society,” Vemula said.The guidelines book, to be made available on the IAP website, is expected to serve as a reference for physiotherapy management of paediatric conditions. IAP women cell member Gargi Tusharika Challa contributed to the cultural committee and physiotherapy slam events.The scientific programme featured workshops, keynote lectures, interactive sessions, panel discussions, research presentations, quizzes and clinical-therapy sessions, facilitating professional collaboration and knowledge sharing among physiotherapists at different stages of their careers.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vijayawada | Silver Rate in Vijayawada | Bank Holidays in Vijayawada | Public Holidays in Vijayawada | Petrol Price in Vijayawada | Diesel Price in Vijayawada | CNG Price in Vijayawada | LPG Price in VijayawadaStay updated with the latest Vijayawada news. articles.title: Plant based menus take seed at colleges
articles.summary: Indian campuses expand plant-based menus: SRM adds vegan cooking to curriculum from 2027, cuts animal products 30%; more colleges offer vegan options for health, sustainability.
articles.body: Canteens are increasingly adding recipes without meat, fish or dairy products.Starting 2027, future chefs at SRM Institute of Hotel Management in Kattankulathur will spend a fifth of their coursework learning to cook without meat, fish, eggs or dairy. The institute has also cut animal products in its dining halls and hostels by 30%, as part of a growing push for plant-based food on Indian campuses.The institution recently collaborated with Humane World for Animals India, which sent professionals to campus to train faculty in plant-based food preparation. “It covered the fundamentals of plant-based cooking, ingredient substitution, menu planning and preparation of dishes without meat, fish, eggs and dairy products,” says Lalitha Shri, vice principal. “We reduced animal products in campus dining and hostels to align practical dining hall practices with classroom learning.”They are not the only ones. Pondicherry University serves plant-based food in its campus canteens and hostels on Tuesdays, so does Bharath Institute of Higher Education and Research (BIHER), Chennai. The German International School in Chennai, one of the first to make a move in this direction, had announced in 2017 that they would serve 100% plant-based meals to their students and avoid using animal products on campus.At BITS Pilani, Hyderabad, there is a separate vegan counter within the mess, says Parth Gupta, a third year student, and joint secretary of the Club for Animal Rights and Equality. “In our case, nearly half the mess menu was plant-based. It took some time to convince the administration, but eventually they agreed to introduce such an alternative. The mess vendors were willing to prepare vegan alternatives for curries with milk or other dairy products such as soya chunks or cashew-based cream,” says Parth.In India, especially in South India, much of vegetarian food is plant-based. However, turning a govt institution’s canteen plant-based is still problematic owing to the political colours it might take on, says Naman Dedhia, of the organisation Plant Based Treaty, which works with educational institutions across the world to teach them about plant-based cuisine. “But there is definitely a movement among private institutions in India.”The dishes are not as bland or unappetising as many imagine, says Sheetal Ahuja, director of Vision International School of Excellence, Ankleshwar, Gujarat, where the canteen went vegan three years ago. “We worked closely with a nutritionist and put a lot of thought into the menu. We experimented with different combinations and cuisines to ensure that the children received good sources of protein, essential amino acids, fibre and other nutrients.”In order to not make children feel that something had been taken away from them, they adapted familiar foods. “We marinated tofu to give it a paneer-like texture. We introduced soy curd, soy lassi, almond milk, kheer and several other nutritious and tasty desserts,” she says. “We talk to children about the compassion behind these choices. Many of them are happy that in their own small way, they can contribute to creating a better world for animals.”At SRM, the practical sessions exposed students to ingredients such as vegetables, fruits, grains, pulses, legumes, nuts, seeds, coconut and plant-based dairy alternatives. Students learn how familiar dishes can be recreated using plant-based ingredients while retaining flavour, texture, presentation and nutritional value. “The focus is also on techniques rather than recipes. Students are encouraged to understand how ingredients behave, how flavour can be developed using herbs and spices, how plant proteins can be incorporated into menus, and how locally available produce can be used creatively,” says Lalitha Shri. “Vegan cuisine is not simply about removing animal-based ingredients; it is about reimagining food with creativity, nutrition and sustainability at its heart. The future of hospitality lies in creating food that is delicious, innovative and mindful of both people and the planet.”While plant-based diets are beneficial for the gut and are fibre-rich, Vitamin B12 deficiencies are often not found, which might have to be addressed through supplements, says Mumtaz Khalid Ismael, consultant clinical dietician.“There are also significant environmental benefits,” says Sridhar A, environmental researcher. “Introducing more plant-based meals in schools and colleges as a dietary choice, is an opportunity to reduce the environmental footprint of the food system while shaping sustainable and ethical habits among young people. Food systems contribute more than one third of global greenhouse gas emissions, and evidence shows that diets with less animal-based food can substantially reduce pressures on land, water, biodiversity and climate.”Beyond health and environmental concerns, there is the ethical question, says Sai Vignesh, vegan advocate and founder of the Chennai-based organisation Almighty Animal Care Trust. “If human beings can thrive on a plant-based diet, why should we continue consuming animals? I would say the ethical aspect should remain at the forefront.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: Map 9,000 acres identified for Jamui industrial area in 10-12 days: Samrat
articles.summary: Jamui industrial area: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary orders mapping of 9,000 acres in 10-12 days, clarifying forest vs raiyati land; ethanol plant due 2027.
articles.body: Patna: CM Samrat Choudhary on Saturday asked officials concerned to complete mapping of 9,000 acres identified for an industrial area in Jamui within 10 to 12 days with details clearly showing the extent of forest land and the portion currently under forest cover.Choudhary issued the directions during a visit to Jamui, where he chaired a review meeting and asked officials to compile complete details of the land by Oct 30 and prepare an action plan. Jamui district magistrate Navin informed the CM that nearly 9,000 acres had been identified in Chakai block. Of this, around 5,000 acres belong to the department of environment, forest and climate change, while 4,000 acres fall under raiyati and other categories.The CM also ordered a detailed assessment of the actual status of the 4,000 acres of raiyati and other-category land. He asked the administration to prepare a work plan to expand public facilities at Lachhuar Mandir and arrange accommodation for devotees.Reviewing law and order, Choudhary asked officials to strengthen policing and ensure regular patrolling. He asked the DM and SP to visit police stations and review their functioning. He also directed officials to prepare a public awareness campaign on de-addiction, along with continued police action and administrative alertness.Accompanied by industries minister Shreyasi Singh and transport minister Damodar Rawat, the CM inspected an ethanol plant under construction in Chakai. Officials said production was expected to begin by March 2027.The DM said the plant, being developed on 105 acres, would have a capacity of 1,000 kilolitres per day, producing about 10 lakh litres of ethanol daily.
